---
title: "Treatment assignment"
description: "Choose randomized, selected, or fixed treatment timing."
jupyter: python3
---

Assignment is a separate probability law. It receives panel dimensions and,
when present, observed and latent unit features. It returns an $N \times T$
binary treatment matrix.

## Choose an assignment family

| Scientific design | Primitive | Main inputs |
|---|---|---|
| One fixed treated cohort | `SingleCohortAssignment` | treated unit positions, adoption period |
| One randomized cohort | `RandomizedSingleCohortAssignment` | cohort size, adoption period |
| Fixed staggered adoption | `StaggeredAdoption` | unit-to-period map |
| Randomized staggered adoption | `RandomizedStaggeredAdoption` | periods and cohort sizes |
| Binary selection | `BinaryLogitAssignment` | observed and latent logit coefficients |
| Sparse binary selection | `SparseLogitAssignment` | selected covariate indices and coefficients |
| Multiple adoption categories | `GeneralizedPropensityAssignment` | category-specific logits |

Use randomized assignment to study estimator behavior under known overlap. Use
feature-dependent assignment to study confounding or conditional identifying
assumptions. Use fixed assignment to reproduce a specific schedule.

## Common simulation components

The examples below share the same features, untreated outcome, and treatment
effect. Only the assignment law changes.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from pypanelsim import core, primitives

dimensions = core.PanelDimensions(n_units=240, n_periods=48)
features = primitives.GaussianUnitFeatures(
    n_observables=2,
    n_unobservables=1,
)
outcome = primitives.SumOutcomeModel(
    models=(
        primitives.TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome(noise_scale=0.4),
        primitives.LinearFeatureOutcome(
            level_coefficients=(1.0, -0.5),
            trend_coefficients=(0.0, 0.0),
            source="observables",
        ),
        primitives.LinearFeatureOutcome(
            level_coefficients=(0.8,),
            trend_coefficients=(0.0,),
            source="unobservables",
        ),
    )
)
effect = primitives.LinearRampEffect(slope=0.12)

def make_simulator(name, assignment):
    return core.PanelSimulator(
        name=name,
        dimensions=dimensions,
        feature_model=features,
        assignment=assignment,
        outcome_model=outcome,
        effect_model=effect,
    )
```

## Randomized assignment

One cohort starts treatment in period 30:

```{python}
randomized = make_simulator(
    "randomized_single_cohort",
    primitives.RandomizedSingleCohortAssignment(
        n_treated=96,
        adoption_period=30,
    ),
).simulate(seed=42)

print(randomized.treated_units.size)
print(randomized.adoption_times[randomized.ever_treated][:5])
```

For staggered adoption, give one size for each adoption period:

```{python}
staggered = make_simulator(
    "randomized_staggered",
    primitives.RandomizedStaggeredAdoption(
        adoption_periods=(24, 30, 36),
        cohort_sizes=(32, 32, 32),
    ),
).simulate(seed=42)

print(sorted(set(staggered.adoption_times[staggered.ever_treated])))
```

These laws sample without replacement. Any unit not sampled is never treated.

## Selection with a binary logit

For unit $i$, `BinaryLogitAssignment` uses

$$
P(A_i=1 \mid X_i,U_i)
= \operatorname{logit}^{-1}
\left(\alpha + X_i'\beta + U_i'\gamma\right).
$$

Here $X_i$ is observable to the estimator and $U_i$ is latent.

```{python}
selected = make_simulator(
    "selected_single_cohort",
    primitives.BinaryLogitAssignment(
        adoption_period=30,
        intercept=-0.3,
        observable_coefficients=(0.8, -0.4),
        unobservable_coefficients=(0.9,),
    ),
).simulate(seed=42)

print(selected.treated_units.size)
print(selected.unit_covariate_names)
```

The same latent feature affects untreated outcomes and assignment. The design
therefore has unobserved selection by construction.

## Multiple adoption categories

`GeneralizedPropensityAssignment` assigns each unit to never treated or to one
of several adoption periods. Its logits compare each treated category with the
never-treated reference category.

```{python}
multi = make_simulator(
    "selected_staggered",
    primitives.GeneralizedPropensityAssignment(
        adoption_periods=(24, 30, 36),
        intercepts=(-0.8, -0.6, -0.9),
        observable_coefficients=(
            (0.8, 0.0),
            (0.0, -0.7),
            (0.4, 0.4),
        ),
        unobservable_coefficients=((0.6,), (0.3,), (-0.4,)),
    ),
).simulate(seed=42)

print(sorted(set(multi.adoption_times[multi.ever_treated])))
```

The selected category is stored as the unit annotation
`assignment_category`.

## Visual comparison

The following panels use the same feature and outcome laws. Their treatment
patterns differ because assignment changes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-assignment-comparison
#| fig-cap: "A common outcome law under randomized, selected, and staggered treatment assignment."
#| fig-alt: "Four pairs of heatmaps compare outcomes and treatment under randomized, observed selection, latent selection, and staggered assignment."

assignment_panels = {
    "Randomized cohort": randomized,
    "Randomized staggered": staggered,
    "Selected cohort": selected,
    "Selected staggered": multi,
}

figure, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(12, 13), constrained_layout=True)
for row, (label, draw) in enumerate(assignment_panels.items()):
    order = np.argsort(draw.adoption_times, kind="stable")
    outcome_image = axes[row, 0].matshow(
        draw.outcome[order],
        aspect="auto",
        cmap="coolwarm",
    )
    treatment_image = axes[row, 1].matshow(
        draw.treatment[order],
        aspect="auto",
        cmap="Greys",
        vmin=0.0,
        vmax=1.0,
    )
    axes[row, 0].set_title(f"{label}: outcome")
    axes[row, 1].set_title(f"{label}: treatment")
    axes[row, 0].set_ylabel("units, sorted by adoption")
    figure.colorbar(outcome_image, ax=axes[row, 0], fraction=0.025, pad=0.02)
    figure.colorbar(treatment_image, ax=axes[row, 1], fraction=0.025, pad=0.02)
    for axis in axes[row]:
        axis.set_xlabel("period")
plt.show()
```

## Unit-time effect heterogeneity

An effect callable receives the same observed, latent, and time features as the
other components. It returns the complete effect surface. The simulator masks
that surface by realized treatment.

```{python}
heterogeneous_simulator = core.PanelSimulator(
    name="heterogeneous_effects",
    dimensions=dimensions,
    feature_model=features,
    time_feature_model=primitives.GaussianTimeFeatures(1),
    assignment=primitives.RandomizedSingleCohortAssignment(
        n_treated=80,
        adoption_period=30,
    ),
    outcome_model=outcome,
    effect_model=lambda context: (
        (
            1.0
            + 0.45 * context.observables[:, 0]
            - 0.30 * context.observables[:, 1]
            + 0.80 * context.unobservables[:, 0]
        )[:, None]
        * (1.0 + 0.30 * context.time_features[:, 0])[None, :]
    ),
)
heterogeneous_panel = heterogeneous_simulator.simulate(seed=42)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-heterogeneous-effects
#| fig-cap: "Observed outcomes, treatment, and the realized heterogeneous effect."
#| fig-alt: "Three heatmaps show observed outcomes, treatment, and realized heterogeneous effects after sorting units by average effect."

order = np.argsort(heterogeneous_panel.effect_surface.mean(axis=1), kind="stable")
figure, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 4.5), constrained_layout=True)
surfaces = (
    (heterogeneous_panel.outcome, "Observed outcome", "coolwarm", None, None),
    (heterogeneous_panel.treatment, "Treatment", "Greys", 0.0, 1.0),
    (
        heterogeneous_panel.treatment_effect,
        "Realized effect",
        "coolwarm",
        None,
        None,
    ),
)
for axis, (values, title, color_map, lower, upper) in zip(
    axes,
    surfaces,
    strict=True,
):
    image = axis.matshow(
        values[order],
        aspect="auto",
        cmap=color_map,
        vmin=lower,
        vmax=upper,
    )
    axis.set_title(title)
    axis.set_xlabel("period")
    figure.colorbar(image, ax=axis, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02)
axes[0].set_ylabel("units, sorted by mean effect")
plt.show()
```

## Assignment metadata

Every simulated panel records the assignment class and its draw metadata:

```{python}
print(selected.metadata["assignment"]["model"])
print(selected.unit_annotations.keys())
```

Use metadata for audit and diagnostics. Do not infer a study's identifying
assumption from a design name alone. State whether assignment is random,
observed-feature dependent, or latent-feature dependent in each experiment.

See the [primitive API](reference/primitives.qmd) for parameter definitions.
